checks.question: connect
checks.summary: Speaks MCP 2025-11-25 over Streamable HTTP, and still works when a client offers 2025-03-26.

thresholds.when: cannot negotiate 2025-11-25 over Streamable HTTP when the client offers it

source.ref: MCP Toolkit quickstart: 2025-11-25 over Streamable HTTP is required

thresholds.when: fails to initialize or list tools when the client offers 2025-03-26

source.ref: Client lifecycle: the example handshake offers 2025-03-26 (friction log #2)

checks.question: connect
checks.summary: The suites a run judges by are the ones that were locked.

thresholds.when: a locked suite changed since `hearsay lock`

source.ref: docs/03 §Holdouts and the lock

checks.question: connect
checks.summary: A tool list that changes during a session is announced with tools/list_changed.

thresholds.when: the tool list differs between two turns of one session without a declared capability and a notification

source.ref: MCP 2025-11-25 server/tools: list changed notification

checks.question: connect
checks.summary: Every tool the server lists is exercised by at least one visible case.

thresholds.when: a tool in tools/list is neither called nor expected by any visible case

source.ref: docs/05 §Coverage: a suite can only judge what it reaches (D-025)

checks.question: hear
checks.summary: The suite uses every advertised enum value and tries a value outside each numeric bound.

thresholds.when: an enum value of a parameter no visible case uses

source.ref: docs/05 §Coverage: misheard values land on the values nobody tested (D-025)

thresholds.when: a bounded numeric parameter that no visible case tries outside its bounds

source.ref: docs/05 §Coverage: out-of-range values are where schema errors reach the person (D-025)

checks.question: hear
checks.summary: A misheard variant leads to the same effect, a question back, or a reply that says what was heard.

thresholds.when: a variant silently causes a different effect, or claims success without any effect

source.ref: Functional requirements: synonyms and alternate spellings in parameter descriptions and enums

checks.question: hear
checks.summary: Tool names are valid and not confusable with each other.

thresholds.when: a name falls outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}

source.ref: MCP 2025-11-25 server/tools: tool names

thresholds.when: two tools name the same words after synonym folding (set/apply/update, get/list/show, start/create/add, stop/cancel/delete) and plurals

source.ref: Functional requirements: each tool maps to a distinct customer intent

checks.question: hear
checks.summary: Every tool and parameter has a description a model can map speech onto.

thresholds.when: a tool description is missing or under 20 characters, or a parameter has none

source.ref: Functional requirements: clear, unambiguous tool descriptions

checks.question: hear
checks.summary: Input schemas are valid, declare required parameters, and use enums and bounds.

thresholds.when: an inputSchema is not valid JSON Schema, or a required parameter is not declared

source.ref: Functional requirements: valid JSON Schema inputSchema with all required parameters

thresholds.when: a numeric parameter has no bounds, or a closed set is not an enum

source.ref: docs/05 lint.schema_constraints

checks.question: hear
checks.summary: What the suite says should happen, happens.

thresholds.when: an expectation of the case is not met

source.ref: the suite author's expectation (docs/03 §Expectations)

checks.question: wait
checks.summary: Each tool round trip stays under 500 ms.

thresholds.when: a tools/call round trip exceeds 500 ms

source.ref: MCP Toolkit quickstart: round-trip response latency under 500 ms

checks.question: wait
checks.summary: Modeled time to first audio stays within budget. In scripted mode this is a lower bound.

thresholds.when: modeled asr + plan + tools + speak exceeds the budget

source.ref: docs/03 §Latency model

checks.question: listen
checks.summary: No JSON, markup, ids, tool names or tool-description text reaches the spoken reply.

thresholds.when: the reply contains JSON, a markdown table or heading, a URL, a UUID, an internal id, or a tool name

source.ref: Functional requirements: no API codes, tool names, JSON or internal ids in customer-facing responses

thresholds.when: the reply contains 8 or more consecutive words from a tool description

source.ref: docs/05 speak.no_structured_dump

checks.question: listen
checks.summary: Spoken replies stay short enough to listen to.

thresholds.when: the reply is longer than 400 characters (about 30 seconds at 150 words per minute)

source.ref: Functional requirements: voice responses under 30 seconds

thresholds.when: the reply is longer than the budget

source.ref: docs/05 speak.length

checks.question: listen
checks.summary: Lists are short and offer more.

thresholds.when: more than 5 options are read out

source.ref: Functional requirements: at most 5 options, with pagination

thresholds.when: more than the budget are read out without an offer to continue

source.ref: docs/05 speak.lists

checks.question: listen
checks.summary: Error results are one sentence that says what the person can do.

thresholds.when: the error text contains a stack trace, an error code or an internal id

source.ref: Functional requirements: no API codes or technical jargon in customer-facing responses

thresholds.when: the error text is over 200 characters or names no next step

source.ref: Functional requirements: an actionable next step for every error

checks.question: listen
checks.summary: Refusals are ordinary tool results with isError and a spoken sentence, never protocol errors.

thresholds.when: a tools/call is answered with a JSON-RPC error, or with isError text starting "MCP error -32602"

source.ref: Functional requirements: every tool in tools/list must be invocable

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: A consequential action commits only after the person said yes, preferably through elicitation.

thresholds.when: the action commits without an accepted elicitation or a valid verbal token

source.ref: Functional requirements: explicit confirmation before payment, cancellation or deletion

thresholds.when: the action commits through the verbal path on a client without elicitation (a model can hallucinate a yes)

source.ref: docs/06 §Consent tiers

thresholds.when: the server uses the verbal path although the client declared elicitation

source.ref: docs/06 §Consent tiers: the server chose the weaker path

thresholds.when: the client has no elicitation and the server refuses to commit: safe, but unusable on hosts without elicitation

source.ref: docs/06 §Consent tiers

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: A declined or cancelled confirmation changes nothing.

thresholds.when: committed state changes after the person declined or cancelled

source.ref: Functional requirements: explicit confirmation before high-consequence actions

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: The confirmation says what and how much.

thresholds.when: the confirmation question does not state the amount and the items

source.ref: Functional requirements: confirmation with key details

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: A verbal confirmation token is bound, short-lived and single-use.

thresholds.when: the token is not bound to items and amount, lives longer than 60 s, can be replayed, or survives a cart change

source.ref: docs/05 §Verbal confirmation

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: A misheard amount never commits.

thresholds.when: a perturbed amount commits: it was neither refused nor stated in a confirmation the person could decline

source.ref: Functional requirements: explicit verbal confirmation for voice-only transactions

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: Confirmation only when money moves: never for reads, never for what an active mandate already covers.

thresholds.when: a confirmation is asked during a call to a read-only tool

source.ref: Functional requirements: confirmation before high-consequence actions (payment, cancellation, deletion)

thresholds.when: a confirmation is asked for an action that commits nothing inside an active mandate

source.ref: docs/06: grant once, act freely within the limit, confirm only when money moves

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: Annotations tell the truth about side effects.

thresholds.when: a tool declares readOnlyHint: true but two identical reads differ

source.ref: MCP 2025-11-25 server/tools: tool annotations

thresholds.when: a tool changes state without explicit annotations

source.ref: docs/05 lint.destructive_annotated

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: A tool that asks for confirmation has a case where the person says no.

thresholds.when: a tool asks for confirmation (seen or expected) and no visible case declines or cancels it

source.ref: docs/05 §Coverage: the no is the path that must hold (D-025)

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: Under the mandate profile, a tool that takes an amount has a case that goes over the limit.

thresholds.when: a changing tool with an amount or quantity parameter has no visible case refused with LIMIT_EXCEEDED

source.ref: docs/05 §Coverage: the limit is the mandate's point (D-025)

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: Calls that ignore the advertised schema are refused by authorize(), not by the schema.

thresholds.when: a value outside the advertised enum, or an extra field, is not refused with a mandate code

source.ref: docs/06: a schema communicates authority, it never confers it

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: Nothing staged under an older mandate version commits.

thresholds.when: a call naming a stale version is not refused with POLICY_CHANGED, or a line staged before a narrowing commits

source.ref: docs/06 §Lifecycle

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: An expired mandate is refused without any client action, with a spoken sentence.

thresholds.when: a call after expiry is not refused with MANDATE_EXPIRED and a spoken sentence

source.ref: Functional requirements: a clear expiry message after the session

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: Instructions inside tool results do not widen the scope.

thresholds.when: the scope or tool list changes after an injected result, or the compromised model's out-of-scope call is not refused

source.ref: docs/06 §Honest limits

checks.question: agree
checks.summary: A mandate belongs to the person who granted it, across sessions.

thresholds.when: another principal can use the mandate

source.ref: docs/06 §Principal

thresholds.when: a new session of the same principal does not see the mandate

source.ref: Functional requirements: preserve context across the session
